newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-Japan prices seen easier as China deal off.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-Japan prices seen easier as China deal off.

text.p: Japan rubber futures are expected to tread weaker next week amid disappointment that rubber deals between China and Thailand are not likely to take place, Japanese traders said on Friday.
There was market talk that China may buy 80,000 tonnes of Ribbed Smoked Sheet (RSS3) grade rubber for delivery in the second half of this year.
But reports from Bangkok on Wednesday said that Thai traders and rubber authorities were puzzled by the market talk.
"We expect rubber prices to be easier next week since hopes for the China-Thai deals, which would support rubber futures, have now been dented," said an analyst at a commodity broker in Tokyo.
On the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM), benchmark November ended the morning session at 136.5 yen per kg on Friday, against the Thursday close of 137.2 yen.
Similarly, the benchmark November contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 137.0 yen per kg, against 137.4 yen, compared to 137.4 yen on Thursday.
Japanese traders said the possibility that China would buy RSS3 rubber was relatively slim, considering the fact RSS3 prices are high when compared with prices for Standard Indonesian Rubber (SIR).
In addition, China faces an oversupply after high levels of rubber imports in 1996.
On Thursday, the China Chemical Industry News, a Chinese newspaper, said China must control rubber imports to prevent a glut there this year.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered little changed at about 118 U.S. cents per kg on a FOB basis on Friday, compared to 117 U.S. cents on May 26.
In addition to the diminished hopes for the China deals, high domestic rubber stock levels, combined with technical factors, are likely to pressure Japanese rubber futures, traders said.

"Private investors are holding quite hefty long positions in nearby months led by the spot June rubber contract. With the approach of the spot expiry later this month, long-liquidation could dent nearby months," another commodity analyst said.
The expected weakness in nearby months is likely to spill over into other months, he said.

Open interest of Tokyo rubber futures fell to 123,655 lots as of Thursday, compared with 133,758 lots on May 6, as private investors shifted money to more volatile commodity futures such as precious metals.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 149 yen as of Friday, compared with 148 yen on May 26.
